chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Al-Barqi from Sa'd ibn Sa'd Al-Ash'ari from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the Qunut: Is Qunut performed in all prayers, or only in those where recitation is done aloud? He said: 'Qunut is not [performed] except in the morning prayer (Al-Ghadah), Friday prayer, Witr, and Maghrib.'

key_terms.الْغَدَاةِ: The morning prayer (Fajr), often referred to as Al-Ghadah in this context
key_terms.الْقُنُوتِ: Supplication recited during prayer, specifically while standing before bowing

ai.seo_question: In which specific prayers is Qunut performed according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam Al-Rida (AS), the specific scope of the recommended Qunut supplication is delineated, restricting it to Al-Ghadah (Fajr), Al-Jumu'ah, Al-Witr, and Al-Maghrib, thereby clarifying the distinction between general and specific recitations. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on adhering to the Prophet's and Imams' specific practices rather than generalizing acts of worship, highlighting the precision required in ritual prayer (Salah). The limitation to these four prayers underscores the unique spiritual significance attributed to these specific times of worship within the Shia tradition.
